claims.text: Current experimental and computational methods have limited accuracy for determining high-temperature solid and liquid thermodynamic properties across large HEA composition spaces.
Current experimental and computational methods have limited availability of high-temperature solid and liquid thermodynamic-property data across large HEA composition spaces.
Current experimental and computational methods have limited efficiency across large HEA composition spaces.
A CALPHAD-based high-throughput method can rapidly explore thousands of HEA compositions.
CALPHAD can be used to investigate composition and temperature effects on HEA microstructure.
CALPHAD-based high-throughput screening is an efficient tool for designing advanced high-temperature HEAs.
Rapid exploration of composition-dependent and temperature-dependent microstructure will improve the determination of melting and liquid thermodynamic properties.
The intervention will improve thermodynamic-property prediction accuracy relative to current experimental and computational baselines.
The intervention will increase the availability of thermodynamic-property estimates across a large HEA composition space.
The intervention will improve the efficiency of determining thermodynamic properties across a large HEA composition space.
The intervention can accurately determine melting temperatures of multicomponent HEAs.
The intervention can accurately determine enthalpies of fusion of multicomponent HEAs.
The intervention can accurately determine entropies of fusion of multicomponent HEAs.
The intervention can accurately determine volume changes upon melting of multicomponent HEAs.
The intervention can accurately determine liquid thermodynamic properties of multicomponent HEAs.
The intervention is applicable to both high-temperature solid and liquid states of multicomponent HEAs.
The method's performance is limited by CALPHAD accuracy and the availability of reliable thermodynamic databases.
A significant discrepancy between predictions and experimental measurements would falsify the hypothesis.
